lead.headline: Google makes Workspace MCP servers and CLI GA, and from 1 February agents must use them instead of the REST APIs
lead.summary: Google-hosted MCP servers now cover Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat and Tasks, and a Workspace CLI with packaged agent skills serves terminal agents. The catch: AI agents must use MCP rather than calling Workspace REST APIs directly, with enforcement from 1 February 2027. A free Standard tier keeps published quotas; a paid Scaled tier for higher limits starts billing on 1 April 2027. Admins get agent audit logs, DLP and human-confirmation rules.

number_of_day.label: Fully AI-generated tracks Tidal will remove when its ban takes effect on 9 December. It says 43% of uploads in the past 90 days were made entirely by AI.

news.headline: On MCP's second birthday, servers can ship Skills to Claude, and Tasks and Elicitation go GA
news.summary: Skills over MCP (public beta in Claude and Claude Code) lets a server publish playbooks next to its tools, loaded only when needed. Tasks let servers run long jobs in the background, and Elicitation lets them pause for user sign-off: Supabase confirms costs before creating a paid project, Railway asks before removing a service. File Uploads is coming soon.

news.headline: OpenAI says GPT-6 models can design new proteins with only reasoning and code
news.summary: No specialised biology models generate the designs. An internal research model matched or beat specialised models on many design tasks, and in lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT-6.2's designs showed evidence of binding across five targets. Specialised models still helped supply sequences and pick candidates for testing.

news.headline: The EU plans a €50B Sovereign Tech Equity Fund, mainly for AI and quantum companies
news.summary: According to the Financial Times, citing two officials, the fund would make larger, riskier and longer-term bets than existing EU schemes, to cut Europe's dependence on US and Chinese tech. Reuters says it could not immediately verify the report.

news.headline: Amazon buys Decart's AI optimization stack and team, a reported $7.5B bet on Trainium
news.summary: Amazon is buying the technology behind the Decart Optimization Stack and bringing over its three co-founders and engineers. The stack tunes kernels, compilers and runtimes, and Amazon says it will make training and inference on its own chips faster and cheaper as it competes with Nvidia.

x_posts.name: Anthropic
x_posts.text: New Anthropic Fellows research: Returning to the neuron basis for interpretability. Understanding what’s happening inside an AI model helps to make it safer. One obvious place to look is its neurons, or the simple units it’s built from. Early interpretability work did just that,
x_posts.why: Interpretability research going back to individual neurons, the place the field started.

writers_corner.title: Bickering Buildings: A Dialogue Between the Churches of Athens in 1854
writers_corner.take: An anonymous 1854 newspaper satire let Athens' belfries argue over a new Russian-funded bell tower. Magouliotis reads it as a window on the young Greek state's fights over style, foreign influence and its Byzantine past.
writers_corner.quote: Buildings are often thought of as “silent witnesses of history”, but they have a history of talking, especially in moments of crisis.
